# slf4j-extensions

> Kotlin compiler plugin that eliminates SLF4J logging boilerplate by auto-injecting a private `log: Logger` property and 10 inline logging functions into classes. Users write `trace { "message" }` directly — no Logger declaration needed. Lambda is not evaluated when log level is disabled. Supports K1 and K2 compiler pipelines. Works with Kotlin 1.5+, SLF4J 1.7.36+, Java 8+.

Documentation: https://github.com/HarryJhin/slf4j-api-extensions

## The Problem

Every class that logs needs the same boilerplate:

```kotlin
class OrderService {
    private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(OrderService::class.java)

    fun process(order: Order) {
        if (log.isTraceEnabled) log.trace("processing: ${order.id}")
        log.info("order completed")
        log.error("processing failed", exception)
    }
}
```

Logger declaration is repeated in every class. Level-guarded logging requires manual `isXxxEnabled` checks to avoid string concatenation overhead.

## The Solution

```kotlin
class OrderService {
    fun process(order: Order) {
        trace { "processing: ${order.id}" }
        info { "order completed" }
        error(exception) { "processing failed" }
    }
}
```

Zero boilerplate. Lambda is not evaluated when level is disabled.

## Installation

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
plugins {
    id("io.github.harryjhin.slf4j-extensions") version "2.0.0"
}
```

That's it. The plugin auto-adds the runtime dependency.

## Gradle Configuration

```kotlin
slf4jExtensions {
    propertyName = "log"       // Logger property name (default: "log")
    allClasses = true          // Apply to all classes (default: true)
    annotation("com.example.Logged")  // Or filter by annotation
    packages("com.example.service")   // Or filter by package
}
```

## What The Compiler Generates

Source code:
```kotlin
class OrderService {
    fun process() {
        trace { "start" }
        info { "done" }
        error(exception) { "failed" }
    }
}
```

Bytecode-equivalent after compilation:
```kotlin
class OrderService {
    private val log: Logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger("com.example.OrderService")

    private inline fun trace(message: () -> String) {
        if (log.isTraceEnabled) log.trace(message())
    }
    private inline fun trace(throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String) {
        if (log.isTraceEnabled) log.trace(message(), throwable)
    }
    // debug, info, warn, error × 2 — same pattern (10 total)

    fun process() {
        trace { "start" }
        info { "done" }
        error(exception) { "failed" }
    }
}
```

## Target Class Kinds

| Kind | Logger injected | Notes |
|------|----------------|-------|
| `class` | Yes | Primary target |
| `data class` | Yes | May have methods that log |
| `enum class` | Yes | |
| `sealed class` | Yes | Each subclass gets its own logger |
| `object` | Yes | Singleton services |
| `abstract class` | Yes | |
| `interface` | No | No instance state |
| `annotation class` | No | |

## Skip Conditions

1. Class kind is `interface` or `annotation class`
2. Class already has a property with the configured name (default: `log`)
3. Gradle config specifies annotation/package filters and class doesn't match

## `kotlin.error()` Non-Collision

```kotlin
error("msg")    // → kotlin.error(Any) → throws IllegalStateException
error { "msg" } // → injected function → logs at ERROR level
```

Different call syntax (`()` vs `{}`). No ambiguity.

## Runtime Module API

### Logger Extensions (10 functions)

```kotlin
// LoggerExtensions.kt
inline fun Logger.trace(message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.trace(throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.debug(message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.debug(throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.info(message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.info(throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.warn(message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.warn(throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.error(message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.error(throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
```

Pattern: `if (isXxxEnabled) xxx(message())` — lambda not allocated when level disabled.

### Marker Extensions (10 functions)

```kotlin
// MarkerExtensions.kt — accessed via log.info(marker) { "msg" }
inline fun Logger.trace(marker: Marker, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.trace(marker: Marker, throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
// debug, info, warn, error × 2 — same pattern
```

Marker functions are NOT injected by compiler — accessed via `log.info(marker) { }`.

### MDC Utilities (2 functions)

```kotlin
// MdcExtensions.kt
inline fun <T> withMDC(vararg pairs: Pair<String, String>, block: () -> T): T
inline fun <T> withMDC(context: Map<String, String>, block: () -> T): T
```

Sets MDC values for the duration of `block`, restores previous values on exit (exception-safe).

```kotlin
withMDC("requestId" to "abc-123", "userId" to "user-1") {
    info { "processing request" }  // MDC contains requestId + userId
}
// MDC restored to previous state
```

## Modules

| Module | Artifact | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `slf4j-extensions-runtime` | `io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-extensions-runtime` | Inline Logger/Marker/MDC extensions |
| `slf4j-extensions-compiler` | `io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-extensions-compiler` | Compiler plugin (fat JAR) |
| `slf4j-extensions-gradle-plugin` | `io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-extensions-gradle-plugin` | Gradle plugin |

## Compatibility

| Item | Minimum | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| Kotlin | 1.5 | K1 pipeline; K2 for 2.0+ |
| Java | 8 | Runtime target |
| SLF4J | 1.7.36 | Compatible with 2.0 |
| Gradle | 8.0+ | For Gradle plugin |
